tool_input.description: Make all files in dist and uploads world-readable and writable

result:
Done! I've fixed the cross-user permission issue in your CI pipeline. Here's what was changed:

## Summary of fixes:

**1. Updated `publish.yaml` workflow** with `chmod -R o+w dist/` commands at three points:
   - After `uv build` (line 27) — makes built files world-writable immediately
   - After downloading artifacts in `create-release` job (line 44) — fixes permissions before creating release
   - After downloading artifacts in `publish-pypi` job (line 62) — fixes permissions before publishing

**2. Created `init-permissions.sh`** — a deployment script to ensure both `dist/` and `uploads/` are world-writable at runtime

## Why this fixes the problem:

Files built with default umask are created with mode `644` (owner read/write, group/others read-only). When CI runs as a different user or when the web tier writes to `uploads/`, those processes can't write to files they don't own. The `chmod o+w` adds write permission for "others", making files accessible to any user.

The commit is ready and will prevent permission failures the next time your CI runs.
